Everything that can be said about Hades already has been - an rocking soundtrack, impressive story, fun characterizations of the gods, ridiculous customization are all inarguable assets in its favor. My addition to the discourse is pointing out its welcome contribution to the roguelite genre - your progress is not beholden to the whims of fate and being necessarily screwed out of a victory by a "bad run". While certain boons are certainly more or less synergestic with themselves/your loadout, Hades shines in that it allows for skill to make up the randomness gap - you aren't entirely reliant on drawing a particular card combination or an enemy dishing out unavoidable damage. Proper positioning, timing, and skill can overcome many suboptimal boon pairings.
I would also be remiss not to call attention to the Heat system - the degree of customization one gets in increasing run difficulty is something to be emulated.
Do yourself a favor and play this game. (And remember, when you first beat it, you haven't, actually).

Despite its age, Hades is still a top contender for one of the best roguelikes especially for its niche and how well-made it is despite comparison to newer games. Hades somehow blends combat, storyline (as expected of any game) but also romance perfectly and believe me when i say that you'll be disappointed you couldnt find any other game that could achieve the same result without it getting corny or feeling like it's a drop in quality.

my own review after 30+ runs is that the combat doesnt get too repetitive even if you run the same weapon for all of your runs like i do with the shield.. there's a whole bunch of options to choose from (duos boons, cast/special builds) and the next run will never feel like the last, despite similar choices. There are also rewarding upgrades the more runs you do, though it gets repetitive if you play only for the roguelike, which is where the story and thanatos walks in.

I wont go too much into detail but im a sucker for cute relationships and i also enjoy the option of having meg as a romance option so i can decline. It is very very motivating knowing there's this death incarnate dude trying to impress you on random runs, and YES we're all equipping his keepsake. The storyline may be a tiny bit lackluster for some as it's locked behind dozens of runs and is fairly simple, the attractiveness of it is determined by how interested you are towards the characters and whether the combat makes up for it or not (which imo it does, the combat is enjoyable and so are the bonds you get to build with than or meg.)

tdlr; normal to good replayability, good character building and story, memorable sound design and decent voice acting, an insanely good introduction to roguelike as someone who's never played these games, thanatos.

This one truly has my attention years after I bought it. 
[many game spoilers (not story-related) up ahead, beware]

First off, I truly enjoyed the roguelike experience despite never before being interested in the genre. Average full 'escape' takes ~25 minutes and yet you find yourself with a new kit each time. Recently I have taken a liking to attempting a run-through with a somewhat useless kit for the sake of it. The more you replay the more proficient you get and, seriously, haven't been a time I stopped because of being bored of gameplay.

Secondly, as a (mediocre) fan to Greek myths since childhood, the interpretations of the Gods here seem very interesting, as well as the concept of the Underworld portrayed. 
// Also enjoyed the weapon aspects like Gilgamesh and Lucifer, that was unexpected but not unwanted.

Overall, regarding the different features of Hades:
1. [b]Gameplay-wise[/b] - well done, whether one prefers a casual run in a week or several escape attempts in a single evening. 
- The God Mode adds to the features that might really help for someone who isn't interested in high difficulty
- Weapons are somewhat repetitive, even with weapon aspects, yet every player can choose their style (whether to charge in or to attack from a safer distance and avoid traps/attacks + add different Boons to it)
- Regarding Boons - sure, there are generally more useful ones as well as some Gods are generally more preferrable than the others, but I wouldn't say you can only beat the game with these Boons and no others.
- Personally I enjoy visiting Chaos and Charon here and now, but Erebus mostly isn't worth the time if you're playing with tight measures in the pact. but perhaps it is just my comfort speaking.

2. [b]Story-wise[/b] - I believe I like every part of it, except for certain moments of being locked out of advancing the reputation.
- Main Story is simple, but its mundanity (in a weird sense of the word) doesn't make it too complicated to comprehend, so I'd say it doesn't force you to memorize all the Greek myths just to understand what's even going on
- And yet, the behavior and dialogue lines thrown here and there bring me joy when I recognize what exactly it is referencing, and make the world itself deeper than simply a game about 'escape from the Underworld'
- Reputation system is intriguing, as side quest stories feel genuinely close to what I would expect from the characters, not nonsensical, not too fast-paced

3. [b]Art-wise[/b] - stunning, honestly.
- the soundtrack is exactly what you want to hear while slashing dozens of mobs, and Orpheus' songs are genuinely captivating + to add about the audio, the voice acting may sometimes feel a little raw, but the emotions are portrayed greatly, as well as distinctiveness of said voices themselves
- level-design and general BG art is also great, it (and character models) feels fully drawn and with a recognizable style in it. What I do not like here is that some levels are of a weird shape and it is not always convenient to navigate through them without rushing around to compare the exits' next rewards, or stepping straight into the fire
- character art is unique, taken into consideration all the characters here are Greek Gods, they are a distinct variety and you wouldn't mix up one with another

All in all, notwithstanding that it may feel stagnant at times where the quests are locked and the runs get a tad repetitive, I wouldn't say it's easy to get bored with Hades, given the endless variations of dialogues after each completed (or failed) run. This game wants you to fail and improve and it genuinely doesn't hurt to be killed in the middle of a run (maybe a little, I absolutely despise the Styx Temple rats because I am very not careful with what I step into).

If you told me a while ago that I’d actually enjoy a roguelike, especially one with this kind of perspective and gameplay, I probably wouldn’t have believed you. But Hades completely changed my perspective on the genre. I never really thought roguelikes were for me, and I definitely didn’t expect to enjoy a game with this top down perspective as much as I did, but Hades makes everything work together so well. The combat is fast, smooth, and incredibly satisfying, with different weapons, abilities, and builds that make every run feel different. Even when you die, it never really feels like wasted time because you’re constantly unlocking new things, learning enemy patterns, getting stronger, and discovering more of the story. 

The game also does an amazing job of making you want to do “just one more run.” You can start playing for what feels like a few minutes, look at the clock, and somehow an entire hour has disappeared. The characters, dialogue, music, art style, and progression all keep you invested even when you’re getting absolutely destroyed by a boss for the tenth time. The perspective might take a little getting used to if you normally play third-person or first-person games, but once the combat clicks, it feels incredibly natural.

Honestly, I think Hades is one of the best introductions to both hack and slash and roguelike games. It showed me that a genre I never expected to like could actually be insanely fun when done right. And if you can grab it on sale, it becomes an even easier recommendation because you’re getting a ridiculous amount of content for the price. If you’ve never really played roguelikes before and want a game that can completely change your opinion of the genre, Hades is 100% worth trying.

I've played around 55 hours between the Steam and Switch versions and this is such a lovely game in every way. 

Great fast paced and frenetic gameplay with quite a lot of build variety as well as really satisfying progression systems. 

Beautiful art all around, from both the enviroment art to the incredible character designs and portraits. 

On the sound front the game is also great, the music all sounds really good and fits everything perfectly (though I could maybe have done with a few more tracks in some areas for variety but not a big problem) and the voice acting is top tier! That combined with the writing (both the quality and variety) makes all the characters super interesting and likeable and makes it a joy to hear what they have to say every time they pop up! The story is relatively simple but not in a bad way at all, it's a simple plot but that serves for a great gameplay loop and where the depth comes from the characters and their personal stories and relations to what's going on.

The only real bigger criticism I can think of is that I felt the enviroments got kinda repetitive after a point but that's about it.

Grinding in video games is not something I usually sign up for, nor do I show any special interest in it, honestly. Despite having this thought, Hades showed up as an exception for me. Today, while writing this review, I am just a few trophies away from the Platinum, and still, even if I start another run, it would feel as fresh as it was in the beginning.

I got this game when I was, well, unemployed, probably a very weird phase. I had just completed my graduation, no job, no college, nothing. I got this game, and it acted as an escape for me. Fast forward four months, now I am pursuing higher education with a decent part-time job, and thus I decided to lean back towards the game which was there during my worst time. (Alongside Hollow Knight.)

This game pushes you to try different possibilities and execute them accordingly. The variety of choices is actually pretty dope! Movement and controls are smooth, hack and slash is satisfying af! It's not that difficult gameplay-wise, but at the same time, not that easy either. It's not like some normal hack-and-slash games which would want you to keep smashing your controller until you get to the next level. Yeah, for those who just wanna chill, this smashing thing can work, but if you're going for Platinum, then nah.
The main story is kinda interesting too. We work as an intermediary to forge the bonds between the Gods and Goddesses of the Underworld, and that's some really good concept. Also, the amount of side content this game has to offer is notable. One can seriously get hooked just trying to achieve those side feats.

Overall, I had a good time in here. I did not realise any downside to this game, truly.

It's a solid 9 from my side!

Hades is a roguelike that actually makes dying feel useful. Each run through the underworld is short, combat is fast and readable, and the boons you pick from the gods meaningfully change how your weapons play. The six weapons and their aspects give you enough build variety that runs do not blur together.

What sets it apart is the story. Dialogue updates almost every time you die, characters remember what you did, and the plot keeps moving even when you fail. It never feels like filler between attempts.

It is polished, the art and music hold up for dozens of hours, and the difficulty can be tuned once you start clearing. The early game is a bit slow until the mirror unlocks pile up, and if you hate repetition you will bounce off it. I kept coming back until the credits, then kept playing anyway. I highly recommend this game.

I simply choose to interpret them as a suggestion.

Escaping the Underworld would be a lot easier if this game wasn't so damn good. I actually don't want to.

And the sequel is exponentially better. It does everything this game does right, doubles it, and adds MORE.
